verdict.line: You lose if you trade Q poke into his Cannon stance with no shield banked; you win if you force Hammer-stance brawls or isolate him with R after level 6.

brief.thesis: Jayce's kit is two different lanes stapled together: Cannon stance pokes you down with Shock Blast and an Acceleration Gate from range, while Hammer stance is a melee duel form with a leap and a knockback. Mordekaiser has no dash to close that gap, so the matchup is decided by whether you survive the ranged phase with W (Indestructible) banked and then drag the fight into the Hammer-stance range where your sustain and E (Death's Grasp) pull take over. The 51.4% win rate over 216 games reflects an even lane that swings hard on solo-kill windows, which the data says favor you.

theirWindow.when: Cannon stance, your W shield consumed
theirWindow.what: He's free to fire Shock Blast and drop an Acceleration Gate to poke you with zero return damage. Back off wave, don't walk forward to trade without W (Indestructible) banked, since you have no way to close the gap and just eat free magic-less physical poke.

yourWindow.when: He swaps to Hammer stance to engage
yourWindow.what: Hammer stance means he's committing to melee range with only a leap and a knockback, not a disengage tool. Land E (Death's Grasp) to pull him in before he can knock you back with Thundering Blow, then unload Q (Obliterate) and consume W's shield for the heal.

start.why: 52.8% win rate over 142 games. The passive damage reduction on consecutive hits directly blunts his auto-reset poke from Cannon stance while you wait out levels 1-5.

boots.why: 51.9% win rate over 214 games and 81.7% pick rate. Jayce's damage is physical in both stances (Shock Blast, Thundering Blow, auto-resets), so the flat reduction on basic attacks matters more than magic resist here.

core.why: The slow on Q (Obliterate) and E (Death's Grasp) is the single biggest answer to his kiting between stances — it's what turns your lack of dash into an actual catch.
Sustained omnivamp and the % max-health burn on your toggled passive aura keep you alive through extended Cannon-stance poke exchanges.
44.4% win rate over 18 games on this exact path. Burn damage punishes him for standing in E (Death's Grasp) or W (Indestructible) range instead of kiting.

runes.keystoneWhy: Stacks through the extended trades his poke forces and converts to healing, which is exactly the war of attrition this lane becomes before you can close distance.

summoners.why: 56.1% win rate at 69% pick rate, the standard and highest-usage combo. Ignite closes out the solo-kill windows the data says you already favor once you catch him in Hammer stance or inside R.

playing.title: Bank W before every trade
playing.detail: Never walk up to contest Cannon-stance poke with Indestructible on cooldown — you have no answer to Shock Blast and Lightning Field damage without the shield stored.

playing.title: Punish every Hammer-stance leap
playing.detail: The moment he commits To the Skies! to engage, he's lost his ranged kit for 16/14/12/10/8 seconds. Pull him with E and don't let him disengage back to Cannon stance.

playing.title: Save R for an isolate, not a save
playing.detail: Realm of Death removes his jungler and support from the fight for its duration. Use it to force a true 1v1 after level 6, where your solo-kill edge shows up in the numbers.

playing.title: Track his R (Mercury Cannon/Hammer) cooldown
playing.detail: It's only 6 seconds, so he can flex stances mid-fight. Don't assume a Hammer-stance engage locks him there — watch for a mid-fight swap back to Cannon to disengage.

playing.title: Pull through the Acceleration Gate
playing.detail: If he drops an Acceleration Gate to kite, step through it yourself when chasing — the move speed buff applies to any ally champion who crosses it, including you.

playing.title: Use Q's single-target bonus to end trades
playing.detail: Obliterate's damage is increased against a single enemy, so focus him alone in skirmishes rather than cleaving minions when you want to close out a duel fast.

playing.title: Don't contest early waves at range
playing.detail: Levels 1-5 you're losing the poke war outright per the data's lane-advantage read. Farm safe, let Doran's Shield absorb chip damage, and wait for level 6.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and win rates above are measured from live games on the current patch via OP.GG; the stance-by-stance tactical reading and timing calls are my own analysis layered on top.

stats.opponentTip: Do not fight Jayce when your [W] is on cooldown. Try to fight him in close quarters after reaching level 6 to gain lane control.
